1. Present appeal is by the State, directed against the judgment of acquittal of the accused dated 14.11.2016 passed in Special Case (POCSO) No.3/2013 on the file of the II Addl. Sessions Judge,
Kalaburagi.

2. Heard Sri Gururaj V. Hasilkar, learned High Court Government Pleader for the appellant-State and Sri B.C. Jaka, learned amicus curiae for the accused-respondent and perused the records.
3.

Brief facts of the case which are necessary for disposal of the appeal are as under:
The respondent accused has been charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Section 366, 506, 376 (2)(n)(i) of IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act.

The charge sheet papers reveal that the father of the victim girl lodged an oral complaint which was reduced into written complaint vide Ex.P1 alleging that he resides in the Farm house situated in the land bearing Survey No.81 by the side of the road, leading to Kallur in Hinchgeri village.
He had three sons and three daughters and among them, two sons and two daughters are married.
His youngest daughter is studying in IX Standard at Afzalpur and she used to travel from Afzalpur to Hinchigeri village along with her friends.

As usual, on 8.8.2013 at about 10.00 a.m.,
she went to school but she did not return till late evening.
He was worried and enquired with the friends and relatives, but could not trace the victim girl.
Thereafter, the neighboring land owner Bailappa informed him that he has seen the accused who was working in the land of Siddappa Talwar and the victim girl were proceeding in a bus.
Immediately, he went to Siddappa Talwar and made enquiry and got confirmed that accused was working under him since two years.

Sri Siddappa Talwar, called the accused and made enquiry and came to know that accused has kidnapped the victim girl and he is far away, but he did not furnish further information and terminated the call.
Immediately he made one more call to the accused, but the mobile telephone was put off.
Based on such information, complainant lodged a complaint with the jurisdictional police and case came to be registered in Crime No.159/2013.

After registering the case, detailed investigation has been conducted and Investigation Agency searched for the accused The State Of Karnataka vs Ningappa Kollur S/O Sayabanna on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189839901/
2 and the victim girl.

During such investigation, after tracing the accused and the victim girl,
statement of the victim girl was recorded whereby the Investigation Agency filed the charge sheet against the accused for the aforesaid offences.

4. On receipt of the charge sheet, learned Special Judge took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and after securing the presence of the accused and complying necessary formalities framed charges for the aforesaid offences.
Since the accused pleaded not guilty, trial was held.
5. In order to prove the case of the prosecution, in all 24 witnesses were examined as PWs.1 to 24 and relied on documentary evidence which were exhibited and marked as Exs.P1 to P27.

Thereafter,
accused statement as contemplated under Section 313 Cr.P.C., was recorded by the learned Special Judge, wherein the accused has denied all the incriminatory materials found in the case of the prosecution put to him.
6. Accused did not choose to adduce neither defence evidence on record nor furnish any written submission as is contemplated under Section 313(5) of Cr.P.C.

Thereafter, the learned Special Judge heard the parties in detail and acquitted the accused by holding that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove that the accused has abducted the victim girl and had a forcible sexual intercourse with her.

7. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment, State has preferred the appeal on the following grounds:
"That, the judgment of trial Court is perverse and hence liable to be set aside.

That, the PW-3 victim girl who was studying in 9th std. in High School at Afzalpur,
has clearly stated in her evidence before the Court that the accused has taken her by force and ravished her.

That, the accused took the victim by force to Kadani village to the house of one Ramesh Pujari and there the accused introduced her as is wife and threatened her not me to disclose that reality to anybody.
Thereafter, in their house the accused ravished her continuously from 8 to 16 of the said month.
That, this evidence of prosecutrix is not at all considered by the trial Court.

That, the trail Court has committed an error in disbelieving the victim of PW-3 just because the statement of - victim girl is recorded by police at a later point of time,
That, the trial Court has though come to conclusion that victim is a minor girl disbelieved the prosecution case to the extent of sexual assault on the victim.
Which is not correct as once the minority of the victim is believed her consent or no consent is of no consequence.

That, the trial Court has ignored the decision of Apex Court that, even conviction can be sustained on the sole testimony of prosecutrix even in the absence of corroborative The State Of Karnataka vs Ningappa Kollur S/O Sayabanna on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189839901/
3 evidence as held in Mukesh V/S State of Chhattisgad (2014)10 SCC 327.

8.

Reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, Sri Gururaj V. Hasilkar, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently contended that the Trial Court has mis-directed itself in appreciating the material evidence on record whereby wrongly acquitted the respondent resulting in miscarriage of justice and sought for allowing the appeal.

9. He also contended that the victim girl has supported the case of the prosecution partly and there is no bar to appreciate the evidence of a hostile witness to the extent the witness supported the case of the prosecution and sought for allowing the appeal.
10.

Per contra, learned amicus curiae for the respondent-accused Sri B.C. Jaka supported the impugned judgment by contending that duly constituted Court has rightly appreciated the material evidence on record and passed an order of acquittal by providing sufficient reasons in justifying the order of acquittal and therefore, the appeal may be dismissed.
He also pointed out that the innocence of the accused gets reinforced and therefore, the order of acquittal is justified.
11. He also contended that if two views are permissible in a case, the view which favours the accused has to be taken into consideration.
Therefore, in this appeal, this Court cannot re
- visit into the whole prosecution case and thus sought for dismissal of the appeal.
12. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, the following points would arise for consideration.
(1) Whether the finding recorded by the learned Special Judge in acquitting the accused for the alleged offences is suffering from legal infirmity or perversity and thus calls for interference?
(2) What order?
13. In the case on hand, in order to prove the case of the prosecution, 24 witnesses have been examined.
Among them, PW-3 is the victim girl; PW-2 is the father of the victim girl; PW-4 is the brother of the victim girl.
PW-1 is the person who said to have seen the accused and the victim girl together going in a bus.

PWs.12 to 14 are the relatives of the accused who have been examined on behalf of the prosecution to prove that accused took victim girl to their house representing that The State Of Karnataka vs Ningappa Kollur S/O Sayabanna on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189839901/

PWs.5 and 20 are the Medical Officers who have examined the victim girl and the accused respectively and issued the report and the medical certificate vide Exs.P2 and 22 respectively.
15. PW-7 Head Master of the School, where victim girl was studying, is examined on behalf of the prosecution to prove the age of the victim girl.

20, 21 and 22 are the Investigating Officers.

16. Among the testimony of the aforesaid witnesses, testimony of the doctor who is examined as PW-20 is not - 10 - challenged on behalf of the accused who had issued the potency certificate of the accused.

17. Likewise, the testimony of PW-5 Dr. Jayalakshmi who examined the victim girl and issued the medical report vide Ex.P-2 and final report vide Ex.P-3 which shows that in her examination and the FSL report of the samples collected by her did not show any evidence of recent sexual intercourse.
Doctor has also admitted that other than forcible sexual intercourse, there would be possibility of tear of hymen.
18. Therefore, rightly the prosecution placed its reliance on the testimony of the victim girl, eye witnesses and the circumstantial witnesses.

Among the said witnesses PWs.12 to 14 who are the relatives of the accused in their house, the accused stayed with the victim girl till 15.8.2013 representing the victim girl as the wife of the accused have turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.
19. So is the testimony of neighbors of PW-12 who are examined as PWs.15 and 16.

Though prosecution treated all these witnesses as hostile witnesses and cross examined them by confronting the statements said to have been given by them - 11 - before the Investigating Officer under Section 161 Cr.P.C., no useful material is elicited in such cross-examination to advance the case of the prosecution to any extent.
20. Therefore, the evidence i.e., available to the prosecution to bring home the guilt of the accused is the oral testimony of PWs.1 to 4 and 23.
PW.1 is the witness who intimated the father of the victim girl that he had seen accused eloping the victim girl in a bus.
In his cross-examination, he admits that he had seen neither the victim girl nor her parents visited his house.

His testimony is not of The State Of Karnataka vs Ningappa Kollur S/O Sayabanna on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189839901/

Even assuming that the accused is seen in the company of the victim girl, it would only establish a fact that victim girl and accused were seen together by PW-1 and intimated the same to PW-2.
21. PW-23 is the owner of the agricultural land, wherein the accused was serving as a coolie.
When PW-2 met PW-23 and enquired about the accused, PW-23 said to have called the accused over his mobile telephone.
He denied the suggestion that he has given the contact number of accused to - 12 - PW-2 and over hearing the conversation, PW-2 said to have been made with the accused.

Since he did not support the case of the prosecution in toto, he has been treated as partly hostile and cross examined by the prosecution, but no useful material is elicited in such cross-examination.
22. PW-2 is the father and PW-4 is the brother of victim girl.
Admittedly, these two witnesses are not eye witnesses to the incident where accused after kidnapping the victim girl ravishing her.
They got the knowledge of the kidnapping and ravishing the victim girl through other witnesses.

Therefore, the prosecution relied on the sole testimony of PW-3.
23.
PW-3 no doubt supported the case of the prosecution by stating that the accused cajoled her and took her to his relatives house at Kadani and committed forcible sexual intercourse.
24. In her cross-examination, it is elicited that she developed intimacy with the accused while traveling to the school.

It is also elicited that there are number of hotels, residential shops near the bus stand and accused mis- represented to her that sister of the victim girl is eager to meet - 13 - her and therefore, she believed accused and went along with him as she developed intimacy with him.
It is also elicited that while she was travelling in the bus, she did not inform the co- passengers or conductor that accused is forcibly taking her by the accused.
25. It is also elicited that she spent her time in the very same dress on all those days.

Further, it is elicited that she has no occasion to intimate to neighbors, as wife of Ramesh Poojari used to accompany her even to attend nature call.
26. PWs.2 & 4 supported the case of the prosecution.

PW-2 stated that after she had the knowledge from PWs.1 & 23, he lodged the complaint and after 15 days of lodging the complaint, he was summoned to the Police Station and the police had brought the victim girl to the Police Station and on enquiry he came to know the forcible sexual intercourse accused had with her.
In his cross-examination, it is elicited that accused was not known to him and accused had not visited his house.

sentences.text: The above evidence on record is sought to be re- appreciated by the prosecution to annul the impugned judgment and convict the accused by allowing the appeal.

28. In paragraphs 21, the learned Judge has held as under:
"21. Prosecution relies upon these witnesses to prove about alleged misrepresentation made by accused to take prosecutrix with him and to prove that, there was kidnap with dishonest intention of committing rape.

It is definite case of prosecution that,
accused had developed intimacy with prosecutrix and he misrepresented by stating that, his sister is eager to meet prosecutrix and so telling, her took her in the bus to Mallabad and then in the same bus to Kadani.
So far as accused and prosecutrix staying at Kadani village, except version of prosecutrix and P.W.21/ P.S.I., none other witness have supported story of prosecution.
The P.W.2 and 4 have categorically stated that, accused was not coming to their house nor they used to go to the house of accused.
P.W.4 went ahead and stated that, he never saw prosecutrix and accused conversing with each other.

Though P.W.3 stated that, sister of the accused used to come to her house once in two days, PW.4 has clearly stated that, sister of accused was not coming to his house - 15 - nor prosecutrix used to go to her house.
When P.W.2 to 4 are residing together, in case if sister of the accused used to come that house once in two days as stated by prosecutrix, either P.W.7 or P.W.4 could have noticed it.
But they never asserted said fact.

Through their evidence, they have not testified about accused misrepresenting prosecutrix and taking her with him to Mallabad as per story projected by prosecution and it is only prosecutrix who came up with that story.
She is prosecuting studies and used to go to Afzalpur with other children of her village and also friends.
In the event if at all accused had taken her to Mallabad, somebody might have noticed it but there is no witness.
In case if at all she was threatened when she was alighting from the bus at Mallabad, she could have stated that fact to other passengers or the crew of the bus.
But she has not made any attempt.

At one breath she stated that, mother and wife of Ramesh were not in that house and Ramesh himself used to serve her food, at another teath, she stated that, wife of Ramesh used to accompany her to go to answer 2nd call of nature.
If wife of Ramesh was present in house, there was no question of Ramesh serving her food.
As per her own version, she used to go out of house to answer call of nature and even if it is believed that, wife of Ramesh used to accompany her, nothing prevented -

sentences.text: She does not assert that, whenever she was going to answer natures call, accused also used to come with her and there was continuous threat to her.
She has not made any efforts to escape from Kadani village whenever she used to go out of the house to answer call of nature.

It is not the case of the prosecution that,
accused had made use of any weapon to give threat to the prosecutrix.
Considering the entire evidence on record, it appears that, prosecutrix is not bringing the truth before court and she is hiding truth and as such her evidence is not trustworthy.
She went on improving her version and giving the answers filling up the gap and as per her convenience.
Therefore, her version is not safe to believe that, accused had misrepresented, lured, enticed her and took her lo Kadani village.
When evidence of the prosecutrix is not trustworthy and believable, unblemished, evidence of P.W.2 and 4 who have to gain knowledge from prosecutrix is not of much assistance to the prosecution."

29. It is no doubt true that in a given case, if the testimony of the prosecutrix is trust worthy and reposes confidence in the Court, the same could be made as basis for making an order of conviction for an offence of rape.

But,
- 17 - when there is doubt in the mind of the Court as to the testimony of the prosecutrix, as a rule of prudence, the Court has to look for corroboration.
30. In the case on hand, the learned Trial Judge had the benefit of noting the demeanor of the victim girl during the course of examination of the victim girl.
The answers obtained in the cross-examination by the defence was judiciously analysed by the learned Trial Judge.

Victim girl not raising any alarm if she were to be really kidnapped by the accused as is contended by the prosecution that too when accused has taken her in a public bus to Kadani village is a circumstance that the prosecution has failed to explain.

Further, non intimating the neighbors and relatives of the accused in Kadani village about the forcible sexual intercourse is yet another circumstance where prosecution has failed to offer any explanation.

31. Thus, there is a genuine doubt as to the story of the prosecution entertained by the learned Trial Judge in believing the testimony of the victim girl resulting in looking for corroboration in the case of the prosecution in respect of the shaky testimony of the victim girl as discussed supra.
But, the - 18 - prosecution failed to furnish such strong corroboration so as to make firm the shaky testimony of the victim girl.
32. Therefore, the learned Trial Judge disbelieved the case of the prosecution.

No doubt, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently contended that accused failed to offer any explanation The State Of Karnataka vs Ningappa Kollur S/O Sayabanna on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189839901/
8 nor adduced any rebuttal evidence and therefore, the prosecution case is to be believed and appeal is to be allowed.

sentences.text: 33. It is pertinent to note that statute prescribes the presumption in favour of the prosecution under Sections 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act.

In the case on hand, since the victim girl is a minor,
prosecution can very well fall back on the twin presumptions under Sections 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act.
But, in order to take advantage of the presumption, prosecution must place on record the basic facts so as to draw presumption that accused is guilty of the offence alleged against him.
In other words, the prosecution is required to discharge initial burden so as to shift the burden on the accused to rebut the presumption.

In the case on hand when such test is applied, in view of the foregoing discussion, even after re-appreciation of the material evidence on record, this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution is not successful in discharging its initial burden in toto.

Non raising alarm or non resisting to move away from Afzalpur to Kadani village in a public transport would be sufficient enough to show that the victim girl was not actually eloped by the accused but she voluntarily left to Kadani with the accused.

35. These aspects of the matter, when viewed cumulatively, this Court is unable to agree with the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum so as to form an altogether a different opinion against the impugned judgment.
36. It is settled principles of law that in a given case, if two views are permissible, the view that favours the accused must be preferred.
37. It is equally settled principles of law that prosecution has to travel a long distance between the 'may be proved' and the 'actual proof'.
Any amount of suspicion cannot take the seat of proof.
Further, if an order of acquittal is passed in a given case by a duly constituted Court after full fledged trial, the innocence of the accused gets reinforced.

39. Applying these celebrated settled principles of law, governing the criminal jurisprudence to the case on hand, the prosecutrix evidence is not corroborated by the medical evidence nor other circumstantial evidence.
Oral testimony of PWs.2 & 4 also not sufficient enough to hold that prosecution is successful in establishing the offences alleged against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The doubts in the case of prosecution is genuine.
Such genuine doubt should always enure to the benefit of the accused in a given case.
It is therefore, the learned Trial Judge has recorded an order of acquittal in the impugned judgment.
No doubt, the reasons assigned by the learned Trial Judge to some extent is not exhaustive.
However, that itself would not be sufficient to accept the appeal grounds and set aside the impugned judgment by allowing the appeal.
